Right: the two missing pairs get new accent edges, the diagonals A–E and B–D, so the four selected nodes form a clique; C and F are untouched." width="100%"} Adds edges to form a complete graph (clique) among all selected nodes. For directed graphs, creates edges in both directions. Skips edges that already exist. The method works on the current node selection (the `_ws` suffix means "with selection"), so it is usually chained after a selection method such as `select_nodes()` or `select_nodes_by_id()`. Any edge selection is ignored. It modifies the graph in place and keeps the selection as it was. Typical uses: - turning a group of nodes known to interact as a unit (a protein complex, a team, a set of co-authors) into a clique - completing a partially connected group, since only the missing edges are added - building a clique-expansion of a hyperedge or group membership If fewer than two nodes are selected, nothing happens. The orientation of each new undirected edge (which node is stored as the source) follows the order of the selection and is not meaningful. Each pair is checked against the full edge list, so selecting many nodes in a large graph can be slow. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [**edge_attributes]{.doc-parameter-name} : Optional attributes to set on newly created edges, passed through to `add_edge()`. Use them to tag the added edges (e.g., `kind="clique"`) or to give them a `weight=`. The same values are applied to every new edge; edges that already existed are not changed. With no keyword arguments, the new edges have no attributes. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Self for method chaining. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Adding edges between every pair among $n$ selected nodes yields up to $\binom{n}{2} = \tfrac{n(n-1)}{2}$ new edges in an undirected graph and up to $n(n-1)$ in a directed one, since each pair contributes both directions. Existing edges are left untouched: nothing is duplicated or overwritten, so calling this on a partial clique only fills in the gaps. Any keyword arguments are copied onto every new edge, which is a natural way to tag a freshly-materialized clique with a shared label, weight, or type. ## Examples {.doc-examples} Selecting three unconnected nodes and fully connecting them creates the three edges of a triangle. The keyword arguments become attributes on each new edge: ::: {#b701025c .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph() graph.add_nodes(['A', 'B', 'C']) # Create clique among selected nodes id_a = graph.get_id_from_label('A') id_b = graph.get_id_from_label('B') id_c = graph.get_id_from_label('C') (graph .select_nodes_by_id([id_a, id_b, id_c]) .fully_connect_nodes_ws(**{'type': 'clique', 'weight': 1.0}) ) # For undirected: 3 edges (A-B, A-C, B-C) # Returns 3 graph.count_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 3 ``` ::: ::: On a path `A--B--C--D--E`, selecting the first four nodes and connecting them adds only the three missing pairs. The `kind` column shows which edges are new; the original path edges, including `D--E` outside the selection, are left as they were: ::: {#b2644399 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ec.Graph() graph.add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D", "E"]) graph.add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "D"), ("D", "E")]) ( graph .select_nodes(lambda n: n.label in ["A", "B", "C", "D"]) .fully_connect_nodes_ws(kind="added") ) graph.get_edge_df().select(["source", "target", "kind"]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}
